title: Ratio and Rate: Simplifying, Sharing and Speed
seo_title: Grade 7 Ratio and Rate Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Solve problems in contexts involving ratio and rate, including sharing in a given ratio where the whole is given, and comparing quantities of different kinds (rate) such as speed.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 7 ratio and rate worksheets: simplifying ratios, sharing in a ratio, finding a part, rates and recipes. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Add the parts, find one part, then multiply.
key_sub: Rate: different units. Ratio: same kind.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A ratio compares quantities of the same kind: 12 : 18 = 2 : 3 (÷ 6).
  • To share R500 in the ratio 2 : 3, there are 5 parts: R500 ÷ 5 = R100, so R200 and R300.
  • A rate compares different kinds of quantities: 240 km in 3 hours is 80 km/h.
  • Keep the order of the ratio the same as in the question.

Examples

Example

Share R720 in the ratio 3 : 5

8 parts

R720 ÷ 8 = R90

Answer: R270 and R450

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
One part onlyAdd the parts first.
Wrong way roundKeep the order of the question.
Rate or ratio?A rate has units like km/h.

items.q: The ratio of adults to children is 2 : 5. There are 33 more children than adults. How many people are there altogether?
items.e: The difference is 5 − 2 = 3 parts = 33, so 1 part = 11. Total = 7 parts = 77.

items.q: A car drives 270 km in 3 hours at a steady speed. What is its speed?
items.e: A unit rate is the amount for 1 hour: 270 ÷ 3 = 90 km/h. 810 multiplies instead of dividing, and 267 subtracts.

items.q: A hose fills a 90 ℓ tub in 6 minutes. How many litres does it pour per minute?
items.e: Litres for 1 minute: 90 ÷ 6 = 15 ℓ. 540 ℓ multiplies, 84 ℓ subtracts, and 96 ℓ adds.

items.q: Sibusiso reads 135 pages in 5 days. He reads the same number of pages each day. How many pages a day is that?
items.e: Pages for 1 day: 135 ÷ 5 = 27. 675 multiplies, and 130 subtracts.

items.q: A bus drives at a steady speed. What distance is missing?
items.e: The unit rate is 80 km in 1 h. In 4 h: 80 × 4 = 320 km. 240 adds only one more 80, but 4 h is 2 hours after 2 h. 164 adds 4.

items.q: Megan’s heart beats 18 times in 15 seconds. At this rate, how many times does it beat in 1 minute?
items.e: 1 minute = 60 seconds = 4 × 15 seconds. 18 × 4 = 72 beats per minute. 1 080 multiplies by 60, but 18 beats is for 15 seconds, not 1 second.

items.q: Ravi cycles 21 km in 1,5 hours. What is his average speed?
items.e: Speed = distance ÷ time: 21 ÷ 1,5 = 14 km/h. Check: 14 + 7 = 21 km in 1,5 h. 31,5 multiplies, and 19,5 subtracts.

items.q: Which is the better buy for milk?
c: They cost the same per litre
items.e: Find the price for 1 ℓ. 4 ℓ: R6,40 ÷ 4 = R1,60. 2 ℓ: R3,50 ÷ 2 = R1,75. 4 ℓ for R6,40 costs less per litre, even though its price is higher.

items.q: Which is the best buy for apple juice?
items.e: Price per litre: 1 ℓ is R2,40; 2 ℓ is R4,20 ÷ 2 = R2,10; 500 mℓ is 2 × R1,15 = R2,30, and 3 ℓ is R6,60 ÷ 3 = R2,20. The lowest is 2 ℓ for R4,20.

items.q: A car uses 6 ℓ of gas for every 100 km. How much gas does it use for 250 km?
items.e: 250 km = 2,5 × 100 km. 6 × 2,5 = 15 ℓ. 12 ℓ forgets the last 50 km, and 18 ℓ counts 300 km.

items.q: Ayanda swims 400 m in 8 minutes. Ravi swims 300 m in 5 minutes. Who swims faster?
c: They swim at the same speed
items.e: Metres per minute: Ayanda 400 ÷ 8 = 50 m. Ravi 300 ÷ 5 = 60 m. 60 > 50, so Ravi is faster, even though Ayanda swims farther.
